meta.title: Organisers — Battle for Middle-earth 2026
meta.description: The team preparing Battle for Middle-earth 2026. The people who build Middle-earth — from story through safety to the children's game and the market.

intro.p1: This page introduces the team that prepares and runs the whole weekend of Battle for Middle-earth 2026. It is not a role you register for — the organisers' team forms through long-term arrangements within the community.

p2.pre: If you want to get involved, start as a

organizer.p: The event is organised by Moravian LARP, z. s. The name appears in the footer of every page, and behind it stands a team that has been building Battle for Middle-earth for several editions, along with other larp events.
organizer.register_value: L 12656 with the Regional Court in Brno

roles.intro: The team is divided into several areas. Specific names and faces will be added gradually as we prepare for 2026.
roles.name_placeholder: Specific name: to be filled in

items.title: Lead organiser
items.desc: Leads the event, coordinates the whole team, contact with the organiser (Moravian LARP, z. s.).

items.title: Story and game design
items.desc: Creates the year's story, sides' motivations, quests and game rules.

items.title: Safety and approvals
items.desc: Weapons and costume checks, safety briefing, medic coordination.

items.title: Camp and logistics
items.desc: Site, water, firewood, parking, coordination with the landowner and the village.

items.title: Registration and communication
items.desc: Registration system, e-mails, participant communication, social media.

items.title: Children's game
items.desc: Programme for little adventurers, safety oversight and parent facilities.

items.title: Stalls and market
items.desc: Vendor arrangements, coordination with the U Zeleného draka pub, market atmosphere.

items.title: Photo, video and media
items.desc: Official photographer/videographer, media cooperation, post-event gallery.

roles.alert_rotate: Team roles may differ slightly between editions. Some areas (e.g. children's game, media coordination) are run by the same people repeatedly, others rotate based on availability.
